name: Laminin subunit alpha 2-related muscular dystrophy

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Merosin-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy diagnostic criteria

criteria.description: Congenital hypotonia and muscle weakness presenting in infancy
Absence or severe reduction of laminin alpha-2 (merosin) on muscle biopsy immunohistochemistry
Biallelic pathogenic variants in the LAMA2 gene confirmed by molecular genetic testing
White matter abnormalities on brain MRI supportive but not diagnostic

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital hypotonia and muscle weakness plus either muscle biopsy showing laminin alpha-2 deficiency or biallelic pathogenic LAMA2 variants
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Brain MRI findings and elevated serum creatine kinase support diagnosis but are not definitive.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital hypotonia with severe muscle weakness
searchTerms: severe muscle weakness and low tone from birth
very weak floppy muscles present at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence or severe deficiency of laminin alpha-2 in muscle tissue
searchTerms: severe lack of laminin alpha-2 in muscles
absent laminin protein in muscle tissue

pathognomonic.symptomName: Delayed motor milestones with inability to walk independently

common.symptomName: White matter abnormalities on brain MRI
common.notes: T2 hyperintensities without clinical CNS symptoms
searchTerms: brain MRI showing white matter damage
white matter changes on brain scan

common.symptomName: Respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
searchTerms: respiratory insufficiency due to muscle weakness
difficulty breathing caused by muscle weakness

laboratory: Normal to mildly elevated liver enzymes
imaging: Brain MRI showing diffuse white matter T2 hyperintensities
Muscle MRI may show fatty infiltration and muscle atrophy
genetic: Biallelic pathogenic variants in LAMA2 gene
other: Muscle biopsy demonstrating absence or severe reduction of laminin alpha-2 protein by immunohistochemistry

distinguishingFeatures: Deficiency of alpha-dystroglycan rather than laminin alpha-2
Normal laminin alpha-2 expression on muscle biopsy
Characteristic histopathological features such as nemaline rods or central cores
Usually absence of white matter abnormalities on brain MRI

redFlags: Severe congenital hypotonia with respiratory failure
Rapidly progressive muscle weakness in infancy
Failure to achieve independent ambulation by 2 years of age
references: Mendell JR, et al. Laminin alpha2-related muscular dystrophy. GeneReviews. 2020.
Guicheney P, et al. Merosin-deficient congenital muscular dystrophy: clinical and genetic aspects. Neuromuscul Disord. 1998.
